_template_notes.purpose: Render-free SISIFOS template for feature/feature-propagation experiments: physics-informed relative navigation near a target RSO. Synthetic SatSLAM frontend consumes the GT trajectory + GT body params (inertia, COM, omega) + sensor measurements this generates; it does NOT read rendered images, so 'setup.render_frames' is false here.
_template_notes.how_to_use: Copy this file, rename it (drop the leading underscore), edit ONLY the EXPERIMENT LEVERS below for your regime, then run: python main.py --config configs/<your_config>.json. Leave camera/objects/render blocks as-is for render-free runs.

experiment_levers.trajectory.inertia_config: GT inertia tensor = the primary inertia-OBSERVABILITY axis. inertia_type one of {sphere, cylinder, box, custom}. 'custom' (Jx,Jy,Jz diagonal) is the cleanest knob: near-equal Jx~Jy~Jz = near-spherical = WEAK observability; strongly separated principal moments = STRONG observability. Convention: X=highest inertial axis, Z=lowest. NOTE: for the synthetic frontend the .blend mesh is irrelevant (landmarks are random 3D points), so vary inertia HERE, not via selected_model.
experiment_levers.trajectory.path_mode: Relative-motion regime: 'tumbling' (target spins, full rel-dyn coupling — main case), 'inertial' (CRO/inertial drift, no spin), 'hill' (LVLH/Clohessy-Wiltshire). Tumbling is what exercises the rel-dyn factor + health monitor.
experiment_levers.trajectory.omega_min_deg / omega_max_deg: Tumbling spin-rate band (deg/s); a uniform draw in [min,max] sets |omega|. Slow (0.5-1.5) reduces linearization drift but weakens dynamics excitation; fast (3-5) excites dynamics but stresses the propagator. BOTH null => generator's historical 3-5 override (NOT the 0.5-2 init default).
experiment_levers.trajectory.r_AG_G: GT center of mass offset [x,y,z] (m), COM relative to geometric frame G. COM is a RECOVERED/free parameter on this branch (do NOT pin at GT). Magnitude + dominant axis drive COM observability; align dominant component with the low-inertia/long physical axis for the strongest cue.
experiment_levers.trajectory.R0_const: Nominal target range (m). MATCHED-FOOTPRINT PER-TARGET policy: range scales with the target's long axis so every target presents the SAME apparent pixel size (fairest cross-target inertia/COM comparison). Fixed ratio R_Hubble:R_INTEGRAL = 13:5 = 2.6. Baseline ranges: RF_Hubble (13 m) = 100 m (~65% frame on a wide f~25 mm inspection lens, comfortable tumble/CRO-parallax margin); RF_Integral (5 m) = 38.5 m (~40 m). Both well-resolved (hundreds of px) in the proximity-inspection regime; COM observable for both. For feature-based visual SLAM the target must be RESOLVED -- 9 km = poorly-resolved/unresolved (CubeSat ~30px even on the telescope rig) = NOT a feature-SLAM regime. For the synthetic frontend range is observability-redundant (abstract landmarks), so this is chosen for physical realism + transfer to the real frontend. Default below = 100 m (Hubble); use 38.5 m for INTEGRAL.
experiment_levers.trajectory.tend / tstep: Arc length and integration step (s). Frame count after f2f gating ~ tend/IMAGE_MAX_DT_S. tend=500, tstep=0.1 typically yields a multi-hundred-to-1k-frame arc that clears the convergence transient.
experiment_levers.selected_model: RF_* mesh root. Affects RENDERING ONLY (irrelevant for synthetic frontend). Defaults pull inertia/rotation from modules/spacecraft_defaults.yaml. Known: RF_Hubble (cylinder, near-axisymmetric), RF_Integral (box, cruciform — front-end aliasing), RF_CubeSat12U (custom), RF_Target (unit). If you set inertia_config explicitly it OVERRIDES the model default.
experiment_levers.camera_optics_caveat: The camera block below is a WIDE INSPECTION lens (f=25 mm, px 3.45 um -> f_px~7246) matched to close proximity range. CRITICAL: the synthetic frontend projects landmarks through THESE intrinsics (Config.yaml fx/fy), so the lens MUST match the range or target-scale landmarks fly off-frame (the telescope rig f=650 mm at 100 m projects a 10 m cloud ~27000 px wide on a 5472 px sensor -> tracking starves -> backend marginalization crash). At the matched ranges this lens puts both targets at ~half-frame (Hubble 13 m @ 100 m -> 942 px; INTEGRAL 5 m @ 38.5 m -> 941 px).
experiment_levers.duration_tend_kfInterval: tend=500 s @ tstep/IMAGE_MAX_DT_S=0.1 (fps 10) -> ~5000 frames. Duration is set by the INERTIA-observability timescale = torque-free precession period (measured: ~400-500 s at fast spin 3-5 deg/s for anisotropic inertia, ~1000-2000 s at slow spin, infinite/zero for near-sphere). 500 s covers >=1 precession period for fast/strong cells and clears the convergence transient (~200 KF). The rel-dyn inertia dt-sweet-spot (~1 s) is a SatSLAM RUN knob (FrontEnd.kfInterval~10 at fps 10), NOT a dataset parameter.
experiment_levers.sweep_parameters: Cartesian-product sweep map: '<dotted.path>': [v1, v2, ...]. Each combo generates a dataset. Empty {} = single dataset from base_config. Example sweeps shown (commented via _example key) below.

setup._comment: render_frames=false => skip Blender; trajectory + GT + measurements only (synthetic-frontend ready).

trajectory._comment: EXPERIMENT LEVERS live here. See _template_notes.experiment_levers above.

inertia_config._comment: Inertia-observability lever. 'custom' diagonal is cleanest. These values = anisotropic (well-separated) => strong observability. For a weak-observability (near-spherical) regime set Jx~Jy~Jz.

_example_sweep_parameters._comment: Move into 'sweep_parameters' (and delete this key) to sweep. Cartesian product over all listed paths.
